audit.notes: Checked spec/gen_spec.rs against query/query.sql conjunct by conjunct and clause by clause. FROM: tuples(db, params) builds the bag cross-product supplier x lineitem(l1) x orders x nation via nested flat/map_values (tuples_1..tuples_4), matching the implicit cross join and keeping duplicates as a Seq (bag), consistent with 'each table is a bag' comment. WHERE: where_clause conjuncts match the SQL in order: s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey, o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey, o_orderstatus = 'F' (compared as seq![b'F'], correct for CHAR(1) with no padding per host contract), l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate (both DATE/int, so > is plain int comparison, correct), EXISTS l2 (exists_1: l2.l_orderkey == l1.l_orderkey && l2.l_suppkey != l1.l_suppkey, correctly correlated only to l1, ranging only over lineitem, matching the subquery's own FROM/WHERE with no join to supplier/orders), NOT EXISTS l3 (exists_2 negated: l3.l_orderkey == l1.l_orderkey && l3.l_suppkey != l1.l_suppkey && l3.l_receiptdate > l3.l_commitdate, correctly using l3's own receiptdate/commitdate, not l1's), s_nationkey = n_nationkey, n_name = params.p1 (text-byte equality, consistent with the host contract that CHAR columns and $1 arrive without trailing spaces so byte equality is correct). All columns involved are NOT NULL in schema.sql (every column in nation/supplier/orders/lineitem used by the query is declared NOT NULL), so no NULL/three-valued-logic subtlety applies to any of these predicates, comparisons, EXISTS correlations, or the join/filter conditions; the spec's two-valued boolean WHERE clause is sound for this schema. GROUP BY: group key is s_name only, matching SQL's GROUP BY s_name; group_count sums over tuples sharing s_name, exactly COUNT(*). No HAVING in the SQL, and having() is open spec fn returning true (matches 'true when absent' per the header comment). Aggregate: numwait = group_count = COUNT(*), correct (COUNT(*) counts all tuples regardless of NULLs, which also matches since there is no NULL column being counted differently). ORDER BY: row_lt encodes numwait DESC (b.numwait < a.numwait, i.e. a sorts before b when a's count is bigger) then s_name ASC via bytes_lt, matching ORDER BY numwait DESC, s_name; bytes_lt is justified by the header's C/byte-collation note. LIMIT: limit_rows takes the first 100 rows of the full sorted/deduped answer, matching LIMIT 100; query_result existentially quantifies over a full_result and requires out == limit_rows(full, 100), consistent with SQL semantics (there being exactly one full_result bag/order). Output columns: OutRow{s_name, numwait} matches SELECT s_name, COUNT(*) AS numwait in that order and naming. Types: nation/orders/supplier id and key columns are int (INTEGER NOT NULL in schema, correct); CHAR/text columns are Seq<u8> byte sequences (n_name, o_orderstatus, s_name), matching CHAR semantics with the host's no-trailing-space contract; DATE columns (l_commitdate, l_receiptdate) are int days-since-epoch, sufficient since only ordered comparison (>) is used, no arithmetic on dates is needed by this query so scale/precision is moot. Decimal columns (l_quantity, l_extendedprice, l_discount, l_tax, s_acctbal, o_totalprice) are not read by this spec at all, correctly, since Q21 never references them. Params: Params{p1: Seq<u8>} matches the single $1 parameter (nation name), declared VARCHAR in workload.json and compared against CHAR(25) n_name; the host-contract comment about trailing-space handling for the CHAR/VARCHAR comparison is consistent with standard SQL CHAR padding semantics (pad-and-compare is equivalent to trim-and-compare-without-padding when both sides are stripped of trailing spaces, as documented). The row projections (LineitemRow, NationRow, OrdersRow, SupplierRow) include exactly the columns the query reads from each table (e.g. LineitemRow omits l_partkey/l_linenumber/etc., which the query never uses even inside the l2/l3 subqueries since those only filter on l_orderkey/l_suppkey/l_receiptdate/l_commitdate) -- correct projection pruning. No DISTINCT, CASE, LIKE, IN, or further arithmetic appears in Q21, so those categories are not applicable. Overall the spec is a faithful transliteration of the SQL; found no semantic discrepancies.
